finalists.name: Consecutive Close-Above-Prior-High Exhaustion
finalists.note: Counts consecutive bars whose close exceeds the PREVIOUS bar's high -- a strictly stiffer test than an up close, since the whole prior range was engulfed -- and shorts the first bar the streak reaches its threshold, optionally only beneath a 200 EMA. One entry per streak: the signal fires on the bar the counter crosses the threshold and never while it merely stays there. Covers on the first close beneath the previous bar's low.
finalists.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/1601-1700/1601_Consecutive_Close_High1_Mean_Reversion -- 'counts consecutive closes above the prior high and sells once the count reaches a threshold; position exits when price falls below the prior low; optional 200 EMA filter'

finalists.name: Strong Close Into a New Low
finalists.note: Shorts the bar that breaks to a new N-bar low and then closes in the top of its own range (IBS above threshold) -- a failed flush whose bounce is already spent by the close. Optional 200-EMA downtrend filter and an optional intraday session window given in UTC minutes-of-day. Covers on the first close beneath the previous bar's low, which is a bar-versus-bar test rather than an indicator.
finalists.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/1501-1600/1598_10_Bar_Low_Pullback -- 'Low breaks the previous LowestPeriod bars lowest low; IBS > IbsThreshold (0.85); optional close below EMA200; exit on close below previous low'

finalists.name: Bayesian Run-Length Collapse
finalists.note: Runs Adams-MacKay Bayesian online change-point detection on log returns with a Normal-Inverse-Gamma conjugate prior, and trades the bar on which the MAP run length COLLAPSES instead of incrementing, gated on the posterior putting more than 30% of its mass on a run of five bars or fewer. Direction is read from the new segment, so the rule is agnostic between continuation and reversal.
finalists.source: Adams & MacKay, 'Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection', arXiv:0710.3742 (2007) -- run-length posterior, message-passing recursion, constant hazard.

finalists.name: Net-Edge Admission Gate
finalists.note: Gates a signal on cost rather than on strength. When the base rule fires (close crossing its EMA) three quantities are formed: the AGK EDGE effective-spread estimate over the trailing est_win OHLC bars as a fraction of price, with the Roll half-spread doubled as the fallback when EDGE is undefined; a square-root impact term y_imp*sigma_20*sqrt(Q/V20); and the conditional expected edge, the median forward h_bars log return over every past bar in the trailing edge_look window on which this same signal fired in this same direction, counting only fires at least h_bars old so the outcome was already observable. The trade is admitted only if the expected edge clears hurdle times the round trip, so the identical signal is accepted on a liquid name and refused on an illiquid one at the same dollar size. Cost enters the entry condition, not the P&L accounting.
finalists.source: Ardia, D., Guidotti, E., Kroencke, T.A. (2024), 'Efficient Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Open, High, Low, and Close Prices', Journal of Financial Economics 161:103916 (reference implementation at github.com/eguidotti/bidask); Roll (1984) as restated in Novy-Marx & Velikov, 'A Taxonomy of Anomalies and their Trading Costs' (NBER w20721), p.4; Toth et al. (2011) square-root law for the impact term.

finalists.name: Bertram Cost-Aware OU Band Optimization
finalists.note: SINGLE-SYMBOL ADAPTATION of a multi-symbol idea. The harness supplies one symbol, so the cointegrated second leg is replaced by the symbol's own trailing mean log price: x = log(C) - mean(log C, mu_win). Everything that makes the idea distinct is kept. An AR(1) fit of x gives theta = -log(rho) per bar and the stationary sd; entry a and exit m are then jointly chosen over a grid to maximise the RATE (m - a - cost)/E[T_cycle], with E[T] the exact OU first-passage time (pi^0.5/theta)*(F(w_m)-F(w_a)), F(w) = int_0^w e^(s^2)(1+erf s) ds, verified against the ODE it solves. The full cycle is a->m plus m->a, so capital's idle leg is paid for too. Bertram's Sharpe objective is not offered: at a zero risk-free rate it collapses to sqrt(E[T]/Var[T]), which is independent of the return per cycle and therefore ignores the cost term entirely - the rate objective is the one where cost bites. m* comes out well away from zero, which is the whole point.
finalists.source: Bertram (2010), 'Analytic Solutions for Optimal Statistical Arbitrage Trading', Physica A 389(11); large-scale test with data-snooping controls in Cummins & Bucca (2012), 'Quantitative Spread Trading on Crude Oil and Refined Products Markets', Quantitative Finance. Trade-cycle decomposition T = T1 + T2 and the return function r(a,m,c) = m - a - c reproduced from Krauss (2015), FAU Discussion Paper 09/2015, section 4.2 (equations 22-24).
